We have an international airline looking to license the independent concert documentary for their passenger-entertainment system. The proposed terms are a worldwide, twelve-month, non-exclusive license using the current picture and delivery master. Before I can sign off, I need each of you — rights, music, and post-production leads — to report any approval conditions or concerns you have. Let's hear from rights first.

transcript.text: I need to flag a critical rights issue. I reviewed the executed performer agreements yesterday, and they restrict licensing of the documentary to the United States, Canada, and the United Kingdom only, for a maximum six-month non-exclusive term. The agreements also require a written rights amendment before we can deliver. The buyer's draft proposes worldwide, twelve-month terms that exceed what we're currently cleared for, and that draft arrived after I completed my review. So my approval conditions are: (1) the territory must be limited to the US, Canada, and UK; (2) the term must be reduced to six months; and (3) a written rights amendment must be executed before delivery.
